name: delegation-first
description: The standing delegation directive for a boss–worker agent setup: delegate execution by default and reserve the expensive boss for judgment and review — the posture layer above the delegation-rules calculus

name: delegation-rules
description: The delegation policy layer for fractality bosses: a decidable routing matrix (delegate when verification is cheaper than generation) plus per-model playbooks for the worker fleet

name: fractality
description: An agent operating system in its earliest form: fractality-mission-control (a scheduler daemon holding the agent roster, call tree, and usage metering) plus the fractality CLI, which lets an expensive boss agent delegate tasks to swarms of cheap worker agents running in isolated Claude Code processes under other model providers, exchanging everything through files on disk

name: addressable-specs
description: Addressable specifications: spec:// URIs, stable anchors, and the spec tree layout that lets a human correct an agent in twenty tokens

name: campaign-plans

name: comparative-research
description: Comparative research documents: evergreen competitor studies with two-way gap analysis and numbered roadmap deltas

name: conflict-protocol
description: Conflict resolution for two writers on one file set: Human > Spec > Tests > Code, REVIEW markers, and the conservative-default uncertainty path

name: decision-records
description: Decisions, not facts: record why with data and a revisit trigger, at the spec anchor the decision governs

name: dev-runtime-docs
description: Load-bearing setup + runtime docs: a change to toolchain / prerequisites / env / paths ships with the doc update in the same commit, never deferred

name: discovery-prompt
description: The DISCOVERY collaborative-research prompt: a structured-uncertainty response grammar, adversarial self-checks, and intensity knobs for LLM research sessions

name: git-atomic-commits
description: Atomic commits discipline: one commit = one logical idea — how to split a mixed working tree, when to batch, and why atomicity matters more in a human-AI team (the message FORMAT is the separate conventional-commits flow)

name: git-attribution-policy
description: A deliberate authorship-attribution posture for AI-assisted repositories: human-authored surface by default, with the disclosure alternative documented

name: git-autonomy
description: Commit/push autonomy: routine large changes proceed without a confirmation handshake; a fixed set of non-routine, hard-to-reverse operations (history rewrites, force-push, large blobs, CI/signing/secrets) always stops and asks first

name: git-conventional-commits
description: The Conventional Commits message format: a typed header (type(scope): subject), a why-not-what body, the allowed-type set, scope convention, worked examples, and anti-patterns

name: git-practices
description: Git practices — the family aggregator for a repository's commit-and-push discipline: one install pulls the message format (conventional-commits) and the atomicity discipline (atomic-commits), and — as they land — human-authored attribution and commit autonomy. Content-minimal (PROP-028): no boot snippet of its own; each member ships theirs.

name: health-audit
description: The periodic health audit: a recurring judgment sweep over what the per-commit gate is structurally blind to, recorded as an append-only trend

name: licensing
description: Licensing posture for a product: a proprietary-with-relicense-intent placeholder, permissive-only dependencies, and the EULA-to-open path

name: managed-blocks
description: Managed blocks: how a tool writes into files it does not own — one delimited block, deterministic scanning, hard stop on malformed state

name: manual-tests
description: Human-runnable manual tests: markdown walkthroughs for the integration surfaces automated suites cannot prove

name: multi-user-planning
description: Multi-contributor campaign stewardship with ritual-free session continuation, deterministic goals, and explicit opt-in handoffs

name: omnichannel

name: operating-modes
description: Codeword-triggered operating modes: one safe default posture, explicit opt-in postures, and red lines that survive any mode

name: qualified-naming
description: Qualified naming for package ecosystems: mandatory groups, identity tuples, short names only at the CLI boundary, collision vs conflict

name: redbook
description: The redbook collection: the AI-native development practices, distilled from the book into installable flows — one edition, one tested set

name: secrets-hygiene
description: Secrets hygiene for agent-driven repositories: surface-secrets never printed or persisted, sanctioned process boundaries, and scope discipline

name: source-mirrors
description: Single-writer source mirrors: one mainline, hosts as read-replicas, manifest-driven fast-forward-only fan-out that fails loud

name: spec-genres

name: sync-from-code

name: tool-design-lessons
description: Design lessons for self-updating tools and package systems: pointer-flip activation, immutable instances, identity-is-source, vendor the bootstrap

name: two-process-model
description: The two-process model: human and AI as coprocessors with complementary architectures, files as the only shared memory

name: wal

name: wal-specspaces
